text: On the B-theory of time, the tensed properties past, present, and future are objective, non-relational features that events possess independently of any observer.
explanation: False. The B-theory holds that the only fundamental temporal relations are the tenseless earlier-than/later-than relations, and it treats 'past,' 'present,' and 'future' as indexical, perspectival descriptions, so that 'now' works like 'here.' The view described is the A-theory, which the B-theorist explicitly opposes.
